questions.q: When did Daniel have a dream and visions in his mind?
questions.a: Daniel had a dream and visions while lying on his bed during the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon.

questions.q: In Daniel’s vision, what was stirring up the Great Sea?
questions.a: The four winds of the heavens were stirring up the Great Sea.

questions.q: What came up out of the sea?
questions.a: Four large beasts, each different from the others, came up out of the sea.

questions.q: What was given to the beast that was like a lion?
questions.a: The mind of a man was given to it.

questions.q: What was the bear-like beast told to do?
questions.a: It was told to get up and eat as much meat as it wanted.

questions.q: What was the leopard-like beast given?
questions.a: It was given authority to rule.

questions.q: What did the fourth beast do?
questions.a: The fourth beast devoured, crushed, and trampled what was left with its feet.

questions.q: What did Daniel see happen to the fourth beast as he considered its horns?
questions.a: Daniel saw another little horn grow up among the other ten horns. Three of the first horns were torn out. Daniel saw that the little horn had eyes like a man and a mouth that boasted about great things.

questions.q: Who sat on one of the thrones that was set up?
questions.a: The Ancient of Days sat upon one of the thrones.

questions.q: What business was being conducted by the Ancient of Days?
questions.a: The court was in session and the books were opened.

questions.q: What happened to the four beasts?
questions.a: The beast with the horn that spoke boastful words was killed, its body destroyed, and it was given over to be burned up. The other three beasts had their authority to rule taken away, but their lives were allowed to continue for a time.

questions.q: In Daniel’s vision, who was presented to the Ancient of Days?
questions.a: One who came with the clouds of heaven like a son of man was presented to the Ancient of Days.

questions.q: What was given to this one who was “like a son of man”?
questions.a: Everlasting authority to rule, glory, and a kingdom that will never be destroyed were given to this one who was “like a son of man.”

questions.q: How did Daniel feel because of his vision?
questions.a: Daniel felt very troubled and alarmed because of what he saw.

questions.q: What did Daniel do to understand his vision?
questions.a: Daniel went to one of those standing there and asked him what it all meant, and that one explained the interpretation to him.

questions.q: What was Daniel told the four beasts represented in his vision?
questions.a: Daniel was told that the four beasts were four kings that would arise from the earth.

questions.q: Who will receive the kingdom and possess it forever?
questions.a: The saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever and ever.

questions.q: What did Daniel want to know more about?
questions.a: Daniel wanted to know more about the fourth beast, which was different from all the others, very terrifying, with iron teeth and bronze claws, and which devoured, crushed, and trampled with its feet.

questions.q: What did Daniel want to know about the horns on the fourth beast’s head?
questions.a: Daniel wanted to know about the ten horns and about the little horn that came up and caused three horns to fall, the horn that had eyes and a boastful mouth and looked greater than the others.

questions.q: What did Daniel see the little horn doing to the saints?
questions.a: Daniel saw the horn making war against the saints and defeating them.

questions.q: What happened when the Ancient of Days came?
questions.a: The Ancient of Days came, judgment was given in favor of the saints of the Most High, and the time came for the saints to possess the kingdom.

questions.q: When Daniel asked one standing there about the fourth beast, what did that one say the fourth beast was and would do to the earth?
questions.a: That one said the fourth beast was a fourth kingdom and that it would devour the whole earth, trample it down, and crush it.

questions.q: What did the one standing there say about the ten horns?
questions.a: That one standing there said that ten kings would arise out of the fourth kingdom.

questions.q: What will the one who speaks against the Most High do, and what will be his end?
questions.a: He will oppress the holy people of the Most High. He will try to change the festivals and the law. He will have power over the saints for a time, times, and half a time, but his authority will be taken away and completely destroyed at the end.

questions.q: To whom will the kingdom and dominion under the whole heaven be given?
questions.a: It will be given to the people who belong to the Most High.

questions.q: What was Daniel’s response to this vision?
questions.a: Daniel was greatly alarmed and his face changed in appearance, but he kept the vision to himself.

commentary.text: Daniel's vision of the four beasts. (Dan. 7:1-8) and of Christ's kingdom. (Dan. 7:9-14) The interpretation. (Dan. 7:15-28)

Dan. 7:1-8 This vision contains the same prophetic representations with Nebuchadnezzar's dream. The great sea agitated by the winds, represented the earth and the dwellers on it troubled by ambitious princes and conquerors. The four beasts signified the same four empires, as the four parts of Nebuchadnezzar's image. Mighty conquerors are but instruments of God's vengeance on a guilty world. The savage beast represents the hateful features of their characters. But the dominion given to each has a limit; their wrath shall be made to praise the Lord, and the remainder of it he will restrain.

Dan. 7:9-14 These verses are for the comfort and support of the people of God, in reference to the persecutions that would come upon them. Many New Testament predictions of the judgment to come, have plain allusion to this vision; especially Rev. 20:11,12. The Messiah is here called the Son of man; he was made in the likeness of sinful flesh, and was found in fashion as a man, but he is the Son of God. The great event foretold in this passage, is Christ's glorious coming, to destroy every antichristian power, and to render his own kingdom universal upon earth. But ere the solemn time arrives, for manifesting the glory of God to all worlds in his dealings with his creatures, we may expect that the doom of each of us will be determined at the hour of our death; and before the end shall come, the Father will openly give to his incarnate Son, our Mediator and Judge, the inheritance of the nations as his willing subjects.

Dan. 7:15-28 It is desirable to obtain the right and full sense of what we see and hear from God; and those that would know, must ask by faithful and fervent prayer. The angel told Daniel plainly. He especially desired to know respecting the little horn, which made war with the saints, and prevailed against them. Here is foretold the rage of papal Rome against true Christians. St. John, in his visions and prophecies, which point in the first place at Rome, has plain reference to these visions. Daniel had a joyful prospect of the prevalence of God's kingdom among men. This refers to the second coming of our blessed Lord, when the saints shall triumph in the complete fall of Satan's kingdom. The saints of the Most High shall possess the kingdom for ever. Far be it from us to infer from hence, that dominion is founded on grace. It promises that the gospel kingdom shall be set up; a kingdom of light, holiness, and love; a kingdom of grace, the privileges and comforts of which shall be the earnest and first-fruits of the kingdom of glory. But the full accomplishment will be in the everlasting happiness of the saints, the kingdom that cannot be moved. The gathering together the whole family of God will be a blessedness of Christ's coming.
